hypothesis: Every candidate uses exact (erf) GELU per PROGRAM.mds correctness contract; test whether the cheaper tanh approximation (skips computing erf) both passes the gate and measurably speeds up the FFN.

eval.note: Correctness holds (CPU: max_abs 0.0003-0.0005 on all 13 shapes, well under gate). But GPU speed is a statistical wash, marginally worse: 2.083x vs 2.086x median, 1.921x vs 1.949x geomean. GELU is too small a fraction of total FFN compute (dominated by the two big matmuls) for erf-vs-tanh to matter on this hardware/workload -- both are similarly-fast hardware special functions on A100. Not adopted: zero speed benefit does not justify the added correctness risk of a non-exact activation.

hypothesis: L3: does torch.compile/Inductor max-autotune deduplicate autotuning across the N structurally-identical repeated transformer layers, or does it redundantly re-autotune each occurrence?

eval.note: CONFIRMED: no deduplication. Shape 1 (batch=64,seq=128,d=128,num_layers=4): captured 24 total AUTOTUNE log lines but only 2 DISTINCT shape signatures (addmm(8192x128,8192x128,128x128) and mm(8192x128,128x128)), each occurring 12 times -- i.e. the identical GEMM shape is autotuned separately at every occurrence across the unrolled 4-layer forward, not once. This directly explains (mechanistically, not just observationally) iter 7s shape-14 finding that max-autotune took ~100-300s per matmul kernel x several occurrences and never finished within the 15-min limit: with num_layers=2 and several large-matmul call sites per layer, the redundant per-occurrence autotuning compounds. Does not change any leaderboard number -- v_router2 already avoids routing shape 14 (or any big-batch/big-seq shape) through the compile route for exactly this class of reason, established before this diagnosis. Value is explanatory (real mechanism for the tech report), not a new speedup.

hypothesis: L1: does v_router2 (A100-80-tuned route table) transfer its ranking/performance unchanged to H100? Problem statement allows either GPU.

eval.note: FALSIFIED: route rankings do NOT hold unchanged. This matches the literature reviews own warning: porting an A100 kernel/routing unchanged to H100 and expecting the same ratio is unrealistic -- H100s much higher compute-to-bandwidth ratio changes which route wins per shape (e.g. shape 9: 2.22x on A100-80 amp-fused vs 1.68x on H100; shape 4: 6.50x on A100-80 reduce vs 4.57x on H100). Not re-tuning routes for H100 -- A100-80 remains the canonical leaderboard device (matches primary cluster capacity and existing leaderboard.md/README.md convention); this is documented as an honest cross-architecture finding for the tech report, not acted on further given time constraints.

hypothesis: T7 reopened (real Roofline headroom on shape #8). Survey the actual design space (AddNorm vs fused-FFN-epilogue vs fused-attention+bias) before committing to one kernel, per TODO.mds explicit instruction not to just extend the existing draft.

eval.note: Dispatched a research fork to compare the three PROGRAM.md-listed Triton targets against our actual shape catalog (ffn_dim==d_model in every one of the 14 official shapes). Verdict: AddNorm (fused residual-add + LayerNorm) confirmed as the right first target -- fused-FFN-epilogue has ~2x the theoretical HBM-traffic savings (same-sized ffn_dim intermediate written+reread for GELU today) but requires a competitive fused-GEMM+epilogue kernel that must beat cuBLAS/Inductors already-tuned matmul, meaningfully higher implementation risk than AddNorms reduction+elementwise pattern. Fused-attention+bias ruled out (SDPAs mem-efficient backend is already a highly-tuned library kernel). candidates/v_triton_addnorm.pys design was checked against the standard/textbook Triton LayerNorm-tutorial pattern (fp32-accumulated two-pass mean/var, eps inside sqrt, masked loads/stores, returns both normed output and raw pre-norm sum for the next residual) and confirmed correct -- CPU-fallback path already passes all 13 official shapes (max_abs ~1e-6). Real Triton/GPU correctness+speed still untested. Honest caveat carried forward: expected speed impact on shape #8 is likely modest (GEMM-compute-bound per the 28%-of-peak reading, not bandwidth-bound on add+norm traffic specifically) -- the kernels value is a genuine, correctness-verified custom-kernel contribution, not a claim it closes most of the 72% gap.

hypothesis: L2: does running shape 14s 8 sequential chunks on 2 alternating CUDA streams speed up the forward pass, by letting the scheduler interleave kernels from adjacent chunks when a single chunk doesnt saturate SM occupancy?

eval.shapes_spec: 14 (reduced protocol: warmup=2,repeats=3,rounds=1, same as the original v_chunked14.py probe for direct comparability)
eval.note: FALSIFIED -- pipelining is SLOWER, not faster. opt_ms=79563.05 (2-stream) vs 74606.23 (sequential, v_chunked14.py baseline) -- about 6.6% worse. Confirms the concern already flagged in v_chunked14_streams.pys own docstring: chunks are already GPU-resident (no H2D/D2H transfer to hide, unlike the classic prefetch-while-computing pattern), and each chunk (batch=4, seq=100000) likely already saturates available SM occupancy on its own -- concurrent streams add cross-stream synchronization/allocator overhead without finding real idle capacity to fill. L2 closed: sequential v_chunked14.py remains the better shape-14 implementation; do not adopt the streamed variant.

hypothesis: L2: does running shape 14s 8 sequential chunks on 2 CUDA streams instead of 1 speed up the forward pass?

eval.note: FALSIFIED, real negative result. 2-stream version is 6.6% SLOWER (79.6s vs 74.6s), not faster. Confirms the hypothesis in the candidates own docstring: chunks are already GPU-resident (no H2D/D2H to hide, unlike the classic prefetch-while-computing pattern), and each chunk=4 forward likely already saturates available SM occupancy on its own -- concurrent streams add synchronization/allocator overhead without exposing real parallelism to fill. Reduced timing protocol (warmup=2,repeats=3,rounds=1), same as the sequential baseline for a fair comparison. No further stream-pipelining work planned for shape 14 -- the sequential v_chunked14.py stays the reference implementation.

hypothesis: T7: real Triton/GPU correctness+speed for the AddNorm kernel (fused residual-add + LayerNorm), confirmed as the right target by the earlier research fork.

eval.note: CONFIRMED, broader win than expected. 13/13 correct on real GPU Triton execution (max_abs 0.0006-0.0013, well within 0.002 gate -- higher than the ~1e-6 baseline as expected from the kernels own fp32 reduction having different rounding/associativity than ATen LayerNorm, still comfortably inside tolerance). Geomean 1.88x -> 2.02x (+7.4%) against a TF32-enabled best.py baseline (not yet the full v_router2 stack). Broad-based, not concentrated on one shape: #6 +40%25 (1.75x->2.44x), #8 +21%25 (1.08x->1.31x, notable since #8 was expected to see only modest gains being GEMM-bound), #1 +18%25, #11 +16%25. This is a STANDALONE comparison (plain SDPA attention, no AMP/compile/reduce/fused routing, no B10 mask-cache) -- NOT YET integrated into v_router2, so this number does not change the leaderboard yet. Next: fold AddNorm into v_router2s block implementation (applies orthogonally to routing/precision) and re-verify under AMP fp16 autocast specifically, since the Triton kernels internal fp32-forced accumulation could interact with autocasts dtype policy in ways not yet tested.
